decision_conditions: 1. Time LimitThe development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this permission.Reason: To comply with the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

2. Approved PlansThe development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:* 6744.02/00/01 Rev P2 – Existing Site and Location Plan* 6744.02/00/02 Rev P2 – Existing Site Plan* 6744.02/00/50 Rev P2 – Existing Elevations* 6744.02/02/02 Rev P2 – Proposed Site Plan* 6744.02/02/50 Rev P2 – Proposed Elevations* 6744.02/02/55 Rev P2 – Existing and Proposed Section A-A* 6744.02/02/56 Rev P2 – Existing and Proposed Section B-Band the following supporting document:* Tree Survey Report (Wessex Ecology Ltd, Project No. 6017.3, dated 27 April 2026), except where superseded by details required pursuant to Condition [Arboricultural Method Statement].  Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

3. Arboricultural Method Statement No development, including demolition, site clearance, the delivery or storage of materials, excavation, installation of fencing or any other ground works, shall commence until an Arboricultural Impact Assessment (AIA), Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) and Tree Protection Plan (TPP), prepared by a suitably qualified arboriculturist, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submitted details shall include:a) A Tree Protection Plan in accordance with BS 5837:2012 Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and Construction – Recommendations.b) Details of protective fencing, ground protection measures and exclusion zones.c) A detailed method statement for the installation of the proposed timber and palisade fencing within the Root Protection Areas of retained trees, including measures to avoid damage to roots, procedures where roots are encountered, and measures to prevent concrete leachates entering the rooting environment.d) Full details of all facilitation pruning, including the extent of pruning (in metres), confirmation that the works shall be undertaken by a suitably qualified arborist, and that the works shall accord with BS 3998:2010 Tree Work – Recommendations.e) Details of any arboricultural supervision required during construction.The development shall thereafter be carried out in full accordance with the approved details.Reason: To safeguard the health and longevity of retained trees during construction, in the interests of biodiversity and urban greening, in accordance with Chapter 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework, Policies G5, G6 and G7 of the London Plan, and Policies 79 and 80 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan.

4. Implementation of Tree Protection MeasuresThe approved tree protection fencing and ground protection measures shall be installed before any development commences and shall be retained for the duration of the construction period.No excavation, storage of materials, plant, machinery, chemicals, spoil, fuel or waste shall take place within the protected Root Protection Areas unless expressly approved within the Arboricultural Method Statement.Reason: To protect retained trees during construction in accordance with Chapter 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework, Policy G7 of the London Plan and Policy 80 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan.
description:
External alterations to arches 284 to 285 Lansdowne Road involving
the bricking up an existing arch, installation of replacement roller shutters and
access doors to the front and rear elevations. Raising of the existing rear
lean-to extension by 1.2m and installation of palisade and timber fencing to
the rear boundary.
